stories.title: Eagles' DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks out vs. Cowboys
stories.summary: The Eagles' top two receivers -- DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks -- have been ruled out of Monday night's game against the Cowboys.
stories.detail: PHILADELPHIA -- The Eagles ' top two receivers -- DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks -- have been ruled out of Monday night's game against the Dallas Cowboys . Smith has been dealing with hamstring issues since the summer, when he was sidelined for a portion of training camp. He tweaked his hamstring Week 2 against the Tennessee Titans , saying recently that he thought being dehydrated in the Nashville heat was a contributing factor. He played through the injury the following week but missed the next two games before returning last Sunday against the Carolina Panthers , catching seven balls for 75 yards and a touchdown. Smith was unable to practice this week. Wicks appeared on the practice report this week with an ankle injury. This will be the first time he'll miss a game with the Eagles. Tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) expects to play despite missing the first two days of practice this week. The Eagles' offense could also welcome back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and lineman Landon Dickerson (knee/pec), both of whom are questionable. stories.title: Giants roster moves: Tremaine Edmunds to IR, Paulson Adebo returns
stories.summary: Giants shuffle roster as more injuries hit the defense; Jalin Hyatt elevated from practice squad.
stories.detail: Tremaine Edmunds | Getty Images The New York Giants continue to take hits on defense. The Giants have placed inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, the team’s leading tackler through six games, on injured reserve with a torn chest muscle. The Giants also announced on Saturday that starting safety Jevon Holland, who has a team-high three interceptions, has been downgraded to out with a concussion. Edmunds had 50 tackles in six games. He was second behind rookie Arvell Reese in solo tackles with 34. Micah McFadden, a full-time starter at linebacker for the Giants in 2023 and 2024, will take Edmunds’ place. McFadden played in just one game last season due to a foot injury. The Giants have also lost edge defender Brian Burns, who has 16.5 sacks in 2025, and starting defensive lineman Chauncey Golston for the season. To take Edmunds’ place on the roster, the Giants are activating veteran cornerback Paulson Adebo from injured reserve. Adebo played in just one game before going on IR with a knee injury. stories.title: Packers activate RB Josh Jacobs for 2026 debut
stories.summary: Packers running back Josh Jacobs will make his 2026 season debut against the Lions after spending the first six weeks on the NFL's commissioner exempt list.
stories.detail: GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers running back Josh Jacobs will make his 2026 season debut Sunday against the Detroit Lions after spending the first six weeks on the NFL's commissioner exempt list. Green Bay added him to the active roster from exempt status Saturday. The NFL took Jacobs off the exempt list Monday. The NFL's investigation of Jacobs for potential violations of the personal conduct policy following his arrest earlier this year on misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor destruction of property charges remains active, and a suspension could be equal to or greater than the number of games he already missed. The six games he has missed would be credited toward any suspension. For now, Jacobs is cleared to play. Jacobs pleaded no contest Sept. 10 to the charges resulting from the May 23 incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and reached a deferred judgment agreement on the property damage charge. Without Jacobs, the Packers have had the worst running game in the NFL, ranking last in rushing yards per game at 59.8 yards. stories.title: 49ers activate WR Christian Kirk from IR
stories.summary: The 49ers made a procedural move on Friday, releasing defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo to make room for wide receiver Christian Kirk.
stories.detail: The 49ers made a procedural move on Friday, releasing defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo to make room for wide receiver Christian Kirk. They made things official Saturday. The 49ers activated Kirk from injured reserve to the active roster, and they re-signed Okoronkwo to the practice squad. Okoronkwo and linebacker Jalen Graham were elevated from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Falcons. The team cut defensive lineman Kevin Givens from the practice squad. Kirk has spent the season on injured reserve. He signed a one-year deal with the 49ers in free agency in March and will help Sunday in Mike Evans' absence. The team's top wide receiver was ruled out with Achilles soreness. Kirk, a second-round pick of the Cardinals in 2018, has 432 receptions for 5,415 yards and 30 touchdowns in eight seasons. Okoronkwo, 31, has appeared in all six games with one start this season. He has two tackles and a sack.

stories.title: Best content of the week: Lions CB Rakestraw eager to build on success
stories.summary: Will Burchfield of 97.1 wrote about how Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. is ready to play in a big divisional game.
stories.detail: It wasn’t exactly a storybook beginning for Detroit Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. Be it injuries, bad luck, or a combination of both, he never really had the opportunity to get his NFL career going. However, the past is the past, and Rakestraw, now in his third year in the NFL, has put together a string of solid performances. Will Burchfield of 97.1 has the story on how Rakestraw is happy to be moving in the right direction , but aware that he has more work to do in order to solidify his status as a full-time starter on the Lions’ defense. “I just gotta worry about myself,” Rakestraw said to Burchfield. “If they go get a corner, they go get a corner. Whatever move they make is the best move for the team, so 100 percent behind whatever they want. Obviously we feel like we can do it here, but if they don’t feel like that, they’re the ones who gotta make the big decisions. If we trade for a corner, we don’t know if one of us will be gone or one of us stays, so we just try to stay getting better and better every week, and try to give them a reason to not make that kind of move.” You can read the entire piece from Burchfield right here . stories.title: Vikings activate RB Jordan Mason off injured reserve
stories.summary: The Vikings activated running back Jordan Mason from injured reserve Saturday, completing his recovery from a fractured thumb that required surgery last month.
stories.detail: EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings activated running back Jordan Mason from injured reserve Saturday, completing his recovery from a fractured thumb that required surgery last month. The Vikings had already created a spot for Mason on the 53-man roster Friday by releasing running back DeeJay Dallas , who re-signed Saturday to the Vikings' practice squad and was elevated to the gameday roster for Sunday's matchup against the Indianapolis Colts . Mason is expected to split time against the Indianapolis Colts with teammate Aaron Jones Sr ., who took 90% of the Vikings' running back carries in Mason's absence. "Getting Jordan back, I think will be a really positive thing just because of the offseason he had and the excitement," coach Kevin O'Connell said Friday, after Mason completed a week of practice with no setbacks. "My excitement to see him paired with Aaron, and how we go about the usage there, is going to be an exciting thing because we feel so confident in both of them. But with the workload Aaron's had and the type of warrior he's been, it'll be good to have JP back." teamStories.title: Former Raiders RB Pete Banaszak dies at 82
teamStories.summary: Former Raiders running back Pete Banaszak has died, the team announced Saturday.
teamStories.detail: Former Raiders running back Pete Banaszak has died, the team announced Saturday. He was 82. "The Raiders Family mourns the passing of Pete Banaszak, whose toughness, competitive spirit, and dedication embodied a legendary era of Raiders football and made him a cherished member of the Silver and Black," the team said in a statement. "The deepest condolences of the entire Raider Nation are with Pete's wife Sue, daughters Rebecca and Amy, grandsons Luke, Austin, and Connor, and all of his loved ones." Banaszak played his entire career with the Raiders. The team drafted him in the fifth round of the 1966 AFL Draft, and he retired after the 1978 season. He led the NFL with 16 rushing touchdowns in 1975, which remains a single-season franchise record. He won a Super Bowl XI ring, which was the franchise's first Super Bowl championship. Banaszak appeared in 173 regular-season games with the Raiders and played a central role in the famous "Holy Roller" play. Banaszak, a Wisconsin native, was inducted into the National Polish-American Sports Hall of Fame in 1990.
